claim: The tactic-route report now exposes validated native request, root/direct restore, prefix replay, restore-cost, cache, checkpoint-capture, peak-memory, and logical transition-yield accounting. Persistent worker cache counters are converted to per-job deltas so concurrent seed totals do not double-count cumulative process state.

implementation.cache_result_contract: typed, deny-unknown-fields, request-bound, and validated before its counters enter the report
implementation.resume_policy: older performance checkpoints without restore accounting fail schema validation instead of producing fabricated zero measurements
implementation.useful_transition_definition: a logical proposal outcome that reaches terminal, has positive shaped reward, or reduces goal distance from its shared source
implementation.rate_units: integer millionths; useful_transitions_per_restore_millionths is useful logical proposal transitions divided by native restore samples
implementation.cache_counter_semantics: cache_hits and cache_misses are deltas from the native cache's internal counters; direct_process_local_restore_requests separately counts externally visible direct requests because one request may perform multiple internal cache lookups

scope: This closes explicit P2 restore/replay/cache/memory/transition-yield measurement. The smoke also demonstrates that the current reactive tactic is extremely restore-heavy: 130 native restore samples produced only 12 logical proposal transitions, making tactic execution granularity an explicit P3 throughput target.
